content:
Outgoing Apple CEO Tim Cook's vague comments during an earnings call seem to suggest that heavy use of Siri AI could cost more than we're currently expecting.

Although it's always been clear that we won't get unlimited free Siri AI usage, Cook's comments do seem to point to some bad news…

What we know

Apple aims to handle as much AI processing on-device as possible, both to maximise user privacy and to avoid Apple bearing the server costs for those tasks. However, some tasks will need to run on Apple's own Private Cloud Compute servers, and some will require the use of Google Gemini servers.

Using these servers naturally costs Apple money, so it's always been clear that Apple would apply the same freemium strategy to Siri AI as other companies do with chatbots: a limited free tier, with heavy users paying a monthly fee.

Until now, however, the general assumption has been that subscribing to iCloud+ would be enough to access Siri AI, with usage limits possibly tied to the iCloud+ tier — the 50GB plan gets one cap, the 200GB plan gets a higher one, and the 2TB plan yet another tier higher.

This means many of us would effectively get more generous Siri AI usage bundled into our existing iCloud+ plans.

But we might have to pay more

On the earnings call, Cook was asked about this by Goldman Sachs.

His response seemed to go beyond a simple point about needing an iCloud+ subscription:

One reading is that heavy Siri AI usage won't just require an iCloud+ subscription — it'll require an additional payment on top. In other words, the subscription itself won't automatically grant us higher usage caps; it merely gives us the right to buy add-ons to raise those caps.

His wording is vague, and may not necessarily mean that. However, if Cook simply wanted to say that higher usage caps are included within an iCloud+ subscription, I would have expected him to be clearer. It is precisely the vagueness of his wording that makes me suspect this may not be good news — or at least, taken at face value, that the company hasn't decided yet but is considering an add-on approach.

Of course, none of this matters much until we know what Siri AI usage actually looks like and when we might bump up against those caps. Even if my speculation is correct, it probably won't affect most Apple users. But looking at the existing AI chatbots, for most of us who do find them genuinely useful beyond occasional use, it does tend to end up requiring a paid subscription.

What do you think? Do you agree with my reading of Cook's comments? And if so, do you think you'd find it worth paying to use Siri AI? Share your thoughts in the comments.
